Autostart was enabled that day, and the 12:06 EDT v0.15.0 restart was the first launchd-owned start. Host gates had taken about 13 minutes under a hand-started daemon; the next four all hit the 30-minute limit, and PublishBudgetExceededException fired at 300 seconds. Gate dotnet processes showed scheduling priority 4, the same as backupd, while the plist said ProcessType Background (LaunchdDaemonAutostart.cs:151-152). Removing that key by hand and rebootstrapping moved them to 20 at 14:16 EDT. Check whether gate time then returns to about 13 minutes before daemon started through launchd on macOS runs its gates and agents at launchd\\u0027s standard priority, not background priority\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022The plist \\u0060h9k daemon autostart enable\\u0060 writes carries no ProcessType key, and a test pins that.\u0022,\u0022When \\u0060h9k daemon start\\u0060 goes through autostart on a plist carrying ProcessType Background, the key is removed, every other key and value stays as it was (including the recorded EnvironmentVariables), and the job launchd then runs no longer carries that classification, including a job that was already loaded and idle, so \\u0060h9k update --restart\\u0060 cures an install autostart already wrote. A test pins the removal and the reload.\u0022,\u0022A plist with no ProcessType Background key, including one carrying another ProcessType value, is not rewritten, and its start runs the same launchctl sequence as today. A test pins that.\u0022,\u0022A plist that cannot be read or rewritten does not stop the daemon starting, and the output says the cure was skipped.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Observed 2026-10-30. Autostart was enabled that day, and the 12:06 EDT v0.15.0 restart was the first launchd-owned start. Host gates had taken about 13 minutes under a hand-started daemon; the next four all hit the 30-minute limit, and PublishBudgetExceededException fired at 300 seconds. Gate dotnet processes showed scheduling priority 4, the same as backupd, while the plist said ProcessType Background (LaunchdDaemonAutostart.cs:151-152). Removing that key by hand and rebootstrapping moved them to 20 at 14:16 EDT, and the serialized host gates since then took 14m51s, 13m11s, and 13m09s, so the baseline is back. Priority 20 is launchd\\u0027s standard band, not the 31 of a terminal session; ProcessType Interactive would give 31 and was rejected, so do not add it. The key dates from d9c0b85bd with no recorded reason, and nothing else reads it.\\n\\nWhy the cure sits in LaunchdDaemonAutostart.StartAsync (:80-95): the restart hand-off runs stop, doctor, and start in the newly installed binary (DaemonRestartHandoff.cs:106-110), while h9k update and h9k install run in the old one and never touch the plist. EnableAsync cannot serve either, because it needs the observed environment. Why a reload is needed: launchd keeps the loaded definition. A job loaded and idle, reachable because stop returns early when no daemon is running (DaemonLifecycle.cs:314-338), makes bootstrap fail and falls to kickstart, which measured the old classification with a cured file on disk; only bootout then bootstrap applies it. Bootout is safe here because DaemonLifecycle.StartAsync refuses a running daemon, and Exec does not throw on the nonzero exit an unloaded job gives. Do the removal in plain C#, not plutil, so its test runs on every CI leg (LaunchdDaemonAutostartTests carries no OS gate); the launchctl sequence can be pinned as a generated command list. DaemonLifecycle.cs:128-142 is the existing shape for a repair that must not cost a
